Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

No statutory minimum paid-up capital required for the SL under this pipeline profile; capital may be fixed at a nominal amount and must be fully subscribed and paid-in at subscription, in cash or in kind. No escrow account is required. If capital is set below the historical €3,000 threshold, the SLFS reserve and distribution restrictions apply until capital plus reserves reach €3,000.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

Upon incorporation of the SL, the notary files the deed through the Single Electronic Window (CIRCE/DUE) and the system issues a provisional corporate NIF. Within two months of the deed, the administrator must submit Form 030/036 to the competent AEAT office (or electronically with a digital certificate) to obtain the definitive NIF (one letter identifying the legal form followed by 8 digits, e.g., B-12345678 for an SL), and to register the company in the Census of Entrepreneurs. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment require a separate non-resident NIF (Form 036, 'N' prefix) when holding Spanish assets or executing taxable transactions; the SL itself is the relevant taxable person for Spanish income tax and VAT purposes.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Upon incorporation of the SL, the notary files the deed through the Single Electronic Window (CIRCE/DUE) and the system issues a provisional corporate NIF. Within two months of the deed, the administrator must submit Form 030/036 to the competent AEAT office (or electronically with a digital certificate) to obtain the definitive NIF (one letter identifying the legal form followed by 8 digits, e.g., B-12345678 for an SL), and to register the company in the Census of Entrepreneurs. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment require a separate non-resident NIF (Form 036, 'N' prefix) when holding Spanish assets or executing taxable transactions; the SL itself is the relevant taxable person for Spanish income tax and VAT purposes.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No check-the-box election exists in Spain. The SL is mandatorily a separate taxable person under Ley 27/2014 (LIS). Statutory elections available: (i) consolidated tax group regime (Art. 64 LIS) for groups with ≥75% control; (ii) VAT cash-accounting criteria de caja (Art. 163 decies LIVA) for SMEs with turnover ≤ €2M; (iii) monthly VAT return/refund regime (REDEME, Art. 35 RD 1624/1992) for monthly refund recovery; (iv) One-Stop-Shop (OSS) registration for intra-community distance sales and cross-border B2C digital services; (v) patent-box reduction (Art. 23 LIS) for in-house developed IP. Hybrid-mismatch rules under ATAD (Law 11/2021) apply automatically without elective opt-out.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

0.00 EUR — no de minimis turnover threshold; VAT registration is compulsory upon commencement of any taxable economic activity. An EUR 10,000 OSS threshold applies only to intra-community distance sales to non-taxable persons and is not applicable to B2B DevTools cloud service supplies.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

DevTools/API-monitoring SaaS qualifies for export zero-rating: (i) intra-EU B2B supplies — place of supply is the customer's country (Art. 70 LIVA), invoice must show the customer's valid EU VAT ID and 'inversión del sujeto pasivo' (reverse charge), so no Spanish VAT; (ii) non-EU B2B supplies — Art. 69.1 LIVA places the supply outside Spanish territory, no Spanish VAT applies; (iii) exported physical hardware/appliances qualify for the Art. 21.1 LIVA export exemption with credit (0%) upon customs evidence. Supplies to Spanish-established customers are subject to 21% VAT; the 0% carve-out applies only to customers established abroad.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Export declaration summary record) — required only for physical goods exports; not applicable to pure SaaS/cloud services
  • Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document — required only for physical goods exports; not applicable to digital delivery
  • Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment receipt from the foreign client — AEAT evidentiary practice for zero-rated services

SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): mandatory near-real-time filing of issuance and received VAT records via AEAT web-service APIs (X.509 authentication) within 4 calendar days (8 in July) for large enterprises (turnover > €6M) and REDEME opt-ins. Verifactu (RD 1007/2023): all billing software must be certified, generating QR-stamped, algorithmically verifiable invoices; B2B electronic invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece is phased in from 2025–2026 for enterprises with turnover > €8M. No transactional preprint/digital-stamping clearance is required at standard invoice level.

Spain imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline, but AEAT audit practice treats export payments outstanding beyond 180 days from invoice as presumptive evidence of a domestic taxable supply, triggering reassessment with late interest (Art. 26 LGT) and an infringement surcharge of 50%–150% of the VAT under Art. 191 LGT. Falsified export documentation or abusive zero-rating claims can amount to criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal where defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000 per period, with penalties of imprisonment and full clawback. The complete evidence package (contract, service-rendering logs, VIES validation, client tax-residence certificate, and payment receipts) must be retained for the four-year statute of limitation (Art. 66 LGT).

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Full and unrestricted euro convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive. Spain imposes no general exchange-control authorization for trade, services, or financial flows. The only legal hurdles to profit remittance are documentary: (i) the distributing SL must hold sufficient distributable reserves per audited financial statements; (ii) dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, withholding generally 19%, reduced or eliminated by an applicable Double Tax Treaty or by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where a qualifying EU/EEA parent holds at least 10%); and (iii) statistical and FDI filings must be current. An ISIC 6201 dev-tools cloud business is categorized as Low_Risk_Standard for AML purposes, which materially de-risks convertibility, onboarding, and remittance.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion ratio. The Spanish SL may hold export receipts freely in EUR or foreign currency. Cross-border transaction reporting to the Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistics remains obligatory for operations exceeding the threshold set by applicable Bank of Spain circulars, customarily EUR 50,000 per commercial-services operation; non-compliance produces administrative penalties only and does not invalidate the underlying receipt. The bank ordinarily submits the declaration automatically on the client's behalf.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) — the national central bank and the authority responsible for balance-of-payments statistics and foreign-exchange oversight within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). FX control powers are exercised within the Eurosystem framework, while the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Register), operated by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, administers FDI filings. SEPBLAC, Spain's Financial Intelligence Unit, completes the regulatory perimeter for AML/CTF screening.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Wise Fit: High

Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH. EU-licensed EMIs (Wise, Qonto, Revolut Business, and Spanish EMIs such as Bnext) may open accounts fully remotely and provide SEPA and SEPA Instant IBANs, making them efficient collection and disbursement overlays for recurring subscription billing and small-vendor payments. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a deposit-taking credit institution under Law 10/2010, so it cannot fully substitute for a Banco de España-supervised account for capital escrow, statutory equity compliance, or significant FDI filings; (ii) Mercury, a US-domiciled fintech rather than an EU EMI, is viable only as a USD collection and ACH rail, requiring a US EIN and US Corporate Transparency Act/BOI compliance, and its role must remain subordinate to the Spanish anchor account; (iii) lack of Spanish deposit-guarantee coverage and concentration risk argue against holding the full treasury on an EMI. Recommended structure: one Tier-1 Spanish anchor account, one EU EMI as an operational circuit, and one Mercury USD account as a collection overlay.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident UBO resident in a jurisdiction classified by the European Commission or SEPBLAC as high-risk (including certain LATAM jurisdictions) or involvement of a shell/offshore holding chain.

Root cause: Non-resident UBO resident in a jurisdiction classified by the European Commission or SEPBLAC as high-risk (including certain LATAM jurisdictions) or involvement of a shell/offshore holding chain.

Defense evidence: Certified passport; NIE certificate or application receipt; Hague-apostilled notarized power of attorney addressed to the Spanish bank; clean criminal-record certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales) from the residency jurisdiction; signed PEP declaration; corporate sociograma descending to natural-person UBOs; Spain economic-substance bundle including registered-office lease, payroll records, social-security affiliations, hyperscaler agreements, and client contracts; written commercial explanation of any genuine nexus with the high-risk jurisdiction.
High-value inbound equity injection that is disproportionately large relative to forecast revenue, headcount, and cash burn, triggering source-of-wealth concerns.

Root cause: High-value inbound equity injection that is disproportionately large relative to forecast revenue, headcount, and cash burn, triggering source-of-wealth concerns.

Defense evidence: Notarized Escritura de Ampliación de Capital registered in the Registro Mercantil; sworn statement of lawful source of funds; audited financial statements or personal tax returns of the shareholder covering the remitting account; bank-to-bank reference and account-activity summary from the remitting bank; 24-month treasury forecast; evidence of committed commercial contracts (Stripe MRR report, AWS/Azure/GCP agreements); appointment of a compliance officer under Law 10/2010; company AML risk manual reflecting the Low_Risk_Standard rating.
Frequent outbound disbursements to non-OECD software contractors, data centers, or channel partners located in opaque jurisdictions that do not align with the documented SaaS supply chain.

Root cause: Frequent outbound disbursements to non-OECD software contractors, data centers, or channel partners located in opaque jurisdictions that do not align with the documented SaaS supply chain.

Defense evidence: Signed master service agreements, order forms, and itemized supplier invoices; dated service-delivery evidence including SLAs, uptime metrics, tickets, and logs; PEP and sanctions screening reports for every counterparty; internal treasury approval memoranda; annual AML risk assessment confirming Low_Risk_Standard; segregation-of-duties matrix within finance; VAT-compliant documentation (reverse-charge treatment on B2B cross-border services).
Receipts from cryptocurrency exchanges or virtual-asset service providers (VASPs), use of pre-funded cards, or a shared/virtual-office registered address that fails the economic-substance screen.

Root cause: Receipts from cryptocurrency exchanges or virtual-asset service providers (VASPs), use of pre-funded cards, or a shared/virtual-office registered address that fails the economic-substance screen.

Defense evidence: Commercial contracts proving the underlying software subscription or service; source-of-funds certificates from regulated VASPs; board resolution confirming that the company does not accept crypto-asset payments; registered-office domiciliation agreement and a current utility bill in the corporate name; notarial certificate of the domicilio social; declaration of absence of undisclosed shareholders; Spanish tax filings (Modelo 200, Modelo 303, Modelo 190) evidencing alignment between invoiced revenue, banking flows, and declared taxable base.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Equity route: execute an 'escritura pública de ampliación de capital' before a Spanish notary, deposit the consideration into the designated Capital Escrow or corporate operational account, and transmit via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT with remittance information explicitly reading 'Suscripción y desembolso de participaciones sociales / aportación de capital a ES_SL NIF [company NIF]'. The remitting bank should apply the Banco de España balance-of-payments classification 'direct investment – equity capital' (inversión directa – capital), and the receiving bank must issue the deposit certificate required by the notary. Shareholder-loan route: execute a notarized loan agreement where the term exceeds one year or security is granted, remit under the concept 'préstamo accionista a ES_SL', apply arm's-length interest under Article 16 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law and OECD TP Guidelines, and meet any Spanish source-withholding obligations on interest. Both routes require a post-closing filing with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month (simplified statistical declaration for amounts below EUR 3,005,060.52; full declaration above that statutory threshold). Treasury must reconcile the SWIFT confirmation, the notarial deed, the capital-deposit certificate, and the FDI filing receipt before funds are released for operations.Primary clearing architecture: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) for all EUR vendor and intra-EU settlements within the standard T+1 or SEPA Instant window, carrying a structured creditor reference to avoid reconciliation friction; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR payments (USD, GBP, LATAM currencies), including complete beneficiary details, invoice reference in field 70, and the Banco de España outward-payment statistical code for 'computer services / software subscriptions'; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600, irrevocable, at sight) for LATAM distributors or resellers requiring documentary trade security, with the Spanish Tier-1 bank as confirming/advising bank; (iv) US hyperscaler payments and AWS/Azure/GCP disbursements via SWIFT or via Merchant/Vendor ACH using the Mercury USD account, each matched to the invoice reference; (v) for all operations above the applicable Banco de España reporting threshold, the bank files the automatic IOE/balance-of-payments declaration, and treasury must retain the complete evidentiary file comprising invoices, contracts, delivery logs, and bank confirmations.Deliverable FX Outright Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for hedging recurring USD subscription revenue and cloud-vendor costsFX Vanilla European Options and Zero-Cost Collars covering USD income against EUR operating expendituresFX Swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-dated liquidity bridging between USD receipts and EUR disbursementsNon-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible LATAM currency exposures (e.g., ARS, VES, COP) where physical deliverability is legally or practically unavailableCross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) for long-term intercompany financing and for lag mitigation on large equity subscription inflows

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH. EU-licensed EMIs (Wise, Qonto, Revolut Business, and Spanish EMIs such as Bnext) may open accounts fully remotely and provide SEPA and SEPA Instant IBANs, making them efficient collection and disbursement overlays for recurring subscription billing and small-vendor payments. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a deposit-taking credit institution under Law 10/2010, so it cannot fully substitute for a Banco de España-supervised account for capital escrow, statutory equity compliance, or significant FDI filings; (ii) Mercury, a US-domiciled fintech rather than an EU EMI, is viable only as a USD collection and ACH rail, requiring a US EIN and US Corporate Transparency Act/BOI compliance, and its role must remain subordinate to the Spanish anchor account; (iii) lack of Spanish deposit-guarantee coverage and concentration risk argue against holding the full treasury on an EMI. Recommended structure: one Tier-1 Spanish anchor account, one EU EMI as an operational circuit, and one Mercury USD account as a collection overlay.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general Spanish corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); 15% for qualifying newly incorporated SLs in the first two taxable periods with positive taxable base; 15% reduced rate for certified 'startups' under Law 28/2022 for up to four tax periods, subject to eligibility conditions including lack of prior group listing and annual turnover under EUR 5 million.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% standard Spanish withholding tax for non-resident shareholders (Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes, IRNR), unless a more favourable double taxation agreement or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies. Treaty rates commonly reduce Spanish dividend withholding to 5% for qualifying shareholdings of 10% or 7.5% for portfolio holdings.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The annual Modelo 200 must be filed within 25 calendar days following the expiration of six months after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the statutory window runs from 1 July through 25 July of the following year.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Taxpayer identification: NIF, exact legal name, registered address and founding office data; non-resident representative identifier if a lean structure uses a Spanish director. A non-resident member relying on an SL should maintain a Spanish NIF and identifiable beneficial owner form 099; no local PE is admissible unless fixed place in Spain is shown. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 2 Fiscal period and consolidation indicator: start date and end date of the tax year; sections for APAs and correcting returns. Use the Spanish SL fiscal year rather than parent year; if changing year-end to match US or LatAm parent, file a Modelo 200 with shortened period. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 3 Statement of net turnover amount and principal economic activity code ISIC 6201 / CNAE 6201. Classify ancillary subscriptions and API usage fees under the same CNAE, and do not separate recurring cloud infrastructure revenue into unrelated trade categories. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 4 Prevailing negative tax base offsets claimed from prior periods, including pending net operating loss amounts and the applicable limit formula. For offsetting losses of the pre-merger or pre-transfer period, obtain formal economic-substance evidence and file yearly loss trace schedules. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 5 Positive tax base produced after corrections for permanent differences, integration of double taxation claims, and international tax adjustments. Report any tax base derived from IP royalty or cloud licensing income separately; maintain transfer pricing documentation since related-party transactions are presumed. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 6 Applicable type and coefficient: 25% general, 15% startup/newco, special rates for public listed investment vehicles appropriate to an SL. Certified startup status is ineffective if the commercial owner or directors are shell nominees resident outside Spain; AEAT scrutinises real economic substance. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 7 Total quota and deductions: full income tax due, foreign tax credits, treaty-covered withholding credits, patent box exemption, and capitalisation allowance. Foreign withholding tax on payments received from abroad must be converted on the date of accrual and claimed under ordre public of the DTA if applicable. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.
Box 8 Prepayments, withholdings and instalments already paid; result to be payable on balance sheet or refundable amount. Non-resident shareholders do not include their own tax ID in this box; any Spanish WHT on a bank remittance is handled on the payer's Modelo 200. Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: A Spanish SL must prepare a Local File of related-party transactions where the value of transactions with any related person exceeds EUR 250,000 or regardless of amount when the net turnover exceeds EUR 45 million. A Master File is mandatory for groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 75 million. Form 232 annual related-party disclosure is due where the volume of linked-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000.

Economic substance scope: Spain applies EU ATAD limitations and the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Clause rather than a separate 'ESR' licence. For an SL, economic substance requires that key management and developer decisions, physical premises, risk-taking employees and a demonstrable payroll operate in Spain. Absence of substance abroad can result in CFC inclusion, deemed non-resident PE for permanent employees in LatAm or US jurisdictions, and denial of treaty benefits where a conduit registry fails the principal-purpose test.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion by Concealed Subscription Revenue

Statutory sanction: AEAT may re-characterise revenue with a proportional penalty of 50%-100% of the concealed tax base plus late-payment interest. If the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, Criminal Code Art. 305 applies with prison penalties of two to six years and a fine of six to twelve times the amount defrauded.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly omit income are jointly and severally liable under LGT Art. 42.2; civil restitution to the tax debt may cover principal, surcharge and interest. Criminal proceedings can impose travel bans, surrender of passport, provisional seizure of personal assets and imprisonment.
Shell Company / Artificial Offshore Route

Statutory sanction: General anti-abuse clause disapplies the legal form; related-party transactions are valued under the arm's-length standard; omitted income and imputed payments give rise to a revised tax debt with a 50% to 100% penalty. In hard-core conduit structures AEAT may impose permanent establishment income attribution on the offshore vendor.

Director personal liability: A Spanish court may pierce the corporate veil to reach the Spanish director's personal assets for unpaid tax debts; directors face administrative penalties under the Spanish AML Law for non-transparent beneficial ownership and possible a settlement order in tax fraud proceedings involving shell routing.
AML / Money-Laundering Disqualification

Statutory sanction: Very serious AML violations under Law 10/2010 carry fines up to EUR 1,500,000 (or 10% of the total balance sheet amount) and the mandatory proposal to ESMA/CNMV to revoke the company's payment-institution licence. Criminal conviction under Criminal Code Arts. 301-302 can impose imprisonment of one to four years plus fines of three to five times the disappeared amount.

Director personal liability: Directors are personally liable if they give consent, tolerate or fail to remedy laundering activity; civil conduct includes restitution to Spanish and foreign funds, personal financial sanctions, prohibitions on managing other companies and travel restrictions while subject to an ongoing criminal investigation.
Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Permanent Establishment

Statutory sanction: AEAT may adjust the taxable base under the official comparability standard and impose a 10% surcharge on the adjustment, in addition to default interest. Failure to present the required TP documentation triggers fixed penalties of EUR 3,000 to EUR 10,500 per data item. If the adjustment exceeds EUR 25,000, a penalty of 50% applies in the presence of concealment.

Director personal liability: Directors are personally liable for undisclosed PE activity when the Spanish SL assumes commercial risks of a foreign office through an undocumented server or teleworking arrangement; the company's corporate veil is pierced in respect of unauthorised sub-agent liabilities, and directors may face personal recovery, travel bans if criminal charges are filed and imprisonment in aggravated VAT/tax fraud.
